rule: If `m` is defined only on a superclass that is in the scan, the callee is `Superclass#m`. ... Superclass constructor calls (`super(...)`, `: base(...)`, `: this(...)`, ...) → `Parent#<init>`, constructor.
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type or object name) is method; a class-name call `T(..)` that resolves to a constructor, and `: this(..)` / `: super(..)` / a supertype-list call, are constructor. Kotlin has no `new`; a `val x = T(..)` constructor call is treated as decision A's `= new T(...)`. Secondary constructors delegating with `: super(name)` (line 4) and `: this("rex")` (line 6) are constructor edges from Dog#<init>. `super.speak()` with Animal in the scan names Animal#speak. `eat` exists only on Animal, so `this.eat()` and `eat()` are Animal#eat; `speak` is overridden in Dog, so `this.speak()` is Dog#speak. The header-supertype form `: Base(..)` is covered by case 15.
